title: [Epic base] Shared by every way of building: publish-time checks, build probes, and the published skills' content
body:
epic:#34659#1 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjMnXJdSZifpEN5i7aU

Filing gate: ④ a coordination node under the cross-lane parent #34659 (the 「MCP 二期与问数」 epic), filed on the maintainer's word in this session's chat, 2026-11-18. On the structure, verbatim: 「现在就改结构」; on what this parent restores, verbatim: 「你之前的公共底座不用优化吗」. This session had proposed a shared base and then left it out when it split the epic into lines; this card puts it back.

## What this is

The part of building that belongs to no door. A code-first project, a draft saved over MCP and a hosted build are all judged by the same checks at publish and taught by the same published skills.

**Order: third**, with the MCP build line (#35152), after MCP ask and MCP write (#35176): the draft door's verdict is only as good as the checks behind it. Nothing here is wanted ahead of a queued ask or write card.

## What belongs here

- Publish-time checks for metadata that saves and does not work, in two batches.
- Probes after a build: an empty card, a roll-up that never computed, an unresolved connector action.
- What a refused change names.
- The content and shape of the metadata skills: descriptions that trigger on the task, a router-sized `SKILL.md`, a JSON form in the sections the hosted door serves.
- What a build gets wrong about its own rules, such as seed rows its own validation refuses.

## What does not

- The draft door itself, its version statement, the thin build skill, the build-over-the-door eval: the open MCP door's, on #35152.
- A local flow run from the CLI: code-first, on #35153.
- The hosted build tools' defaults, blueprints and tiers: hosted.

## Why it is its own parent

Hosted build does not wait for the open draft door. It waits for exactly this: when the checks here are in the pin, the hosted rule text that restates them is deleted and the hosted copies of the checks go (objectstack-ai/cloud#4829, objectstack-ai/cloud#4842). This card's state is that gate.

A card here takes its place in the order from the first line that needs it. Code-first authors gain from every check too; that is a benefit, not a reason to move a card ahead.
